Olajengbesi made the allegation in an open letter addressed to elders and stakeholders of Ijesa North, both at home and abroad, in which he urged the people to resist what he described as an attempt to extend the tenure of the incumbent lawmaker, Wole Oke, to 28 years. A copy of the letter was made available to Vanguard in Abuja on Thursday. Recounting his first attempt to join the political race, Olajengbesi said he expressed interest in contesting for the House of Representatives in August 2016, when he was 30 years old and had limited financial resources. He alleged that Hon. Niyi Ajifowobaje, whom he described as one of Oke’s prominent political associates at the time, told him that an aspirant in Ijesa North must be prepared to throw N500 million into a river before considering a contest for the Oriade/Obokun seat. According to him, Ajifowobaje further suggested that an aspirant would need as much as N1 billion to be taken seriously. “I was told to throw away N500 million before running in Ijesa North,” he said. Olajengbesi said he subsequently assembled a group of young people in the constituency on July 11, 2017, to examine the incumbent’s political strengths and identify alternative approaches to representation. He said the group produced a 16-page report, which he had incorporated into a book he was writing. According to him, the report concluded that money was the major political advantage the incumbent brought to the table, rather than ideas, innovation or inspiration for younger generations. “Money was the only thing he was bringing to the table. No ideas, no innovation, no inspiration, no storytelling, nothing to inspire younger people. Just money without excellence,” he quoted the report as saying. He said the report also observed that several professionals and educated people in the constituency were dissatisfied with the quality of representation but were reluctant to support a challenger unless they were convinced the person had sufficient financial resources to sustain the contest. Olajengbesi alleged that the incumbent had cultivated an image of political dominance that made some potential challengers believe they could not compete with his financial strength. He further alleged that Oke once boasted during a private conversation about his election spending and how he had dealt with previous challengers. According to Olajengbesi, Oke allegedly claimed to have paid for the return journeys of some aspirants based abroad and financially settled local contenders. He declined to identify the individuals allegedly mentioned in the conversation. Olajengbesi also alleged that Oke dismissed the capacity of potential challengers, claiming that nobody in Oriade or Obokun could spend even 20 per cent of what he committed to elections. Vanguard could not independently verify the allegations, and efforts to obtain Oke’s reaction were still ongoing as of press time. The Accord candidate said Ijesa North had many respected professionals and business people who had stayed away from politics to protect their reputations. He urged them to reconsider their position, arguing that the withdrawal of people of integrity from politics could leave future generations with a system driven largely by money. “I defeated poverty of the mind a long time ago. I refuse to believe that a young man or woman from Oriade or Obokun must first find a billion naira before anyone will listen to what they have to offer,” he said. He maintained that his campaign was about promoting a different model of political representation in which candidates would be assessed on their records, plans and values rather than their financial capacity. “When I was 30, a man told me to throw N500 million into a river before I could even think of representing my people. I want the next 30-year-old to be asked a better first question. What will you do for Ijesa North?” he said. Olajengbesi urged the people of the constituency to reclaim what he described as their political mandate at the polls. He concluded: “Ijesa North, rise now. On election day, let the self-styled landlord find out who truly owns the mandate. Let’s make his money useless so that we can all say again, ‘Owo ti wo igbo.'” The post 2027: I was told to spend N500m before contesting — Accord Party candidate, Olajengbesi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: INEC must earn voters’ trust before election day — IPC
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The International Press Centre (IPC) has urged officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to build public confidence in the electoral body ahead of the 2027 general elections through transparent conduct, accurate information and effective communication. The Executive Director of IPC, Dr. Lanre Arogundade, said public trust in the commission must be established long before election day, warning that misinformation, disinformation and inaccurate communication could undermine the credibility of the electoral process. Arogundade spoke on Wednesday in Kano at a two-day capacity-building engagement for INEC’s Voter Education and Publicity (VEP) and gender officials on electoral trust, effective communication, legal literacy and voter engagement. He noted that INEC had become a major subject of public discussions surrounding the elections, including disagreements among political parties and their supporters, even when the commission was not directly involved in such disputes. He said the manner in which INEC officials respond to public concerns and clarify issues could either strengthen or weaken confidence in the electoral body. “Every public interaction can either deposit or withdraw institutional trust,” he said. Arogundade explained that the training was designed to deepen the officials’ understanding of the Electoral Act, improve their communication skills, prepare them for crisis situations and equip them with the ability to verify and respond to false information. He stressed that VEP officials must be able to explain electoral laws and procedures in simple language, particularly when disputes arise or tensions develop during the electoral process. He warned that inaccurate responses to questions about electoral laws and voting procedures could damage the commission’s credibility more than withholding an answer. “A vague or inaccurate answer from a VEP official, for example, on legal questions around the Electoral Act or voting procedures can cost the commission more than silence would,” he said. The IPC director also called on INEC to establish dedicated fact-checking units in its state offices to identify and respond promptly to false information circulating about the commission. He said the officials would be introduced to social media listening techniques to monitor conversations about INEC in their respective states and provide clarifications where necessary. Arogundade expressed concern over the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate misleading content, noting that voices could be cloned within minutes and election result sheets falsified within seconds. item.content:encoded: By Hadiza Yusuf The International Press Centre (IPC) has urged officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to build public confidence in the electoral body ahead of the 2027 general elections through transparent conduct, accurate information and effective communication. The Executive Director of IPC, Dr. Lanre Arogundade, said public trust in the commission must be established long before election day, warning that misinformation, disinformation and inaccurate communication could undermine the credibility of the electoral process. Arogundade spoke on Wednesday in Kano at a two-day capacity-building engagement for INEC’s Voter Education and Publicity (VEP) and gender officials on electoral trust, effective communication, legal literacy and voter engagement. He noted that INEC had become a major subject of public discussions surrounding the elections, including disagreements among political parties and their supporters, even when the commission was not directly involved in such disputes. He said the manner in which INEC officials respond to public concerns and clarify issues could either strengthen or weaken confidence in the electoral body. “Every public interaction can either deposit or withdraw institutional trust,” he said. Arogundade explained that the training was designed to deepen the officials’ understanding of the Electoral Act, improve their communication skills, prepare them for crisis situations and equip them with the ability to verify and respond to false information. He stressed that VEP officials must be able to explain electoral laws and procedures in simple language, particularly when disputes arise or tensions develop during the electoral process. He warned that inaccurate responses to questions about electoral laws and voting procedures could damage the commission’s credibility more than withholding an answer. “A vague or inaccurate answer from a VEP official, for example, on legal questions around the Electoral Act or voting procedures can cost the commission more than silence would,” he said. The IPC director also called on INEC to establish dedicated fact-checking units in its state offices to identify and respond promptly to false information circulating about the commission. He said the officials would be introduced to social media listening techniques to monitor conversations about INEC in their respective states and provide clarifications where necessary. Arogundade expressed concern over the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate misleading content, noting that voices could be cloned within minutes and election result sheets falsified within seconds. Also speaking, the Executive Director of the Centre for Media and Society (CEMESO), Dr. Akin Akingbulu, said building public trust required more than issuing public statements, urging INEC to match its promises with concrete actions. “Walk the talk. That is, do what they are supposed to do to deliver a credible election. Be honest with the people,” he advised. Akingbulu also called on the commission to respond promptly to misinformation and disinformation, adding that security agencies, the media and other institutions had important roles to play in ensuring credible elections. In his remarks, the Kano State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Dr. Zango Abdu, said the training was part of INEC’s preparations to ensure its officials were adequately equipped for the 2027 general elections. Abdu said the commission was reviewing lessons from previous elections, identifying challenges and strengthening its operational capacity, logistics and deployment strategies to improve its preparations. He added that the new Electoral Act had provided an opportunity for the commission to improve its operations and the conduct of elections. On voter education, the REC said INEC was collaborating with relevant government agencies, civil society organisations and international partners to increase public awareness and mobilise voters ahead of the polls. He specifically identified the National Orientation Agency (NOA) as one of the commission’s partners, noting that its presence across the 774 local government areas would help expand voter education activities. “Voter education is very crucial. Without voter education, you should forget free and fair elections,” Abdu said. He explained that voters needed to understand their rights, know their polling units and familiarise themselves with the basic rules guiding the electoral process to participate effectively. item.title: How to Style a Pink Buba With a Mini Skirt: Alex Unusual’s Loving Itohan Look
item.description: Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A —popularly known as Alex Unusua l—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt. The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash. Alex Unusual in her contemporary Yoruba buba and mini skirt outfit for the Loving Itohan premiere. She carried the damask into her gele, which was wrapped high into voluminous, sculptural folds. An oversized gold lip-shaped brooch secured one side, adding another detail to the headpiece. Using the same fabric for the skirt and gele also helped bring the different parts of the outfit together, while keeping the pink buba at the centre of the colour story. It’s a styling idea worth borrowing if you’re working with patterned damask and want your accessories to feel connected to the rest of your outfit. Alex Unusual pairs her damask gele with cherub-detailed sunglasses, layered gold jewellery, and custom grillz. Alex’s jewellery and accessories added even more detail. She layered a crystal floral choker with a long gold lariat necklace featuring a stirrup-style drop, then added chunky gold cuff bangles on both wrists and sculptural gold rings. Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. For anyone styling a pink buba, Alex’s choice of accessories offers another useful idea: bring in a second colour from the outfit through your shoes or bag, then use metallic jewellery to tie everything together. She kept her beauty look relatively understated, with defined brows, soft neutral eyeshadow, a hint of emerald liner, and glossy nude lips. Long, neutral-toned nails completed the look. lex Unusual shows off the back tailoring of her fuchsia buba, damask mini skirt, and sculptural gele. item.title: Two French Guards Collapse As Macron Welcomes Slovak President
item.description: Two members of France’s elite Republican Guard collapsed almost simultaneously outside the Elysee Palace as President Emmanuel Macron welcomed his Slovak counterpart, according to televised images and a presidential source. As is customary for the arrival of foreign heads of state, the Republican Guards formed an honour guard in full ceremonial dress with sabres for the arrival of Slovak President Peter Pellegrini late Wednesday. One guard can be seen swaying before crashing to the ground, falling against a pillar at the Elysee Palace as his ceremonial sword clattered to the ground. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (R) bids farewell to Slovakia’s President Peter Pellegrini following their meeting at the Elysee presidential Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume Saligot / AFP) | Guillaume Saligot / AFP Aides and Macron immediately rushed towards the stricken guard, images from an AFP photographer showed. Le Parisien daily said that a second guard collapsed off camera, with Macron looking concerned and then hurriedly welcoming his Slovak counterpart. A French presidential source, who asked not to be named, told AFP that both guards had suffered from “fainting attacks” and no other comment would be made. “Both of them were swiftly taken care of, and everything is fine,” added the source. The Republican Guard, part of the French gendarmerie, is responsible for guards of honour in France, which often involve standing for long periods in heavy clothing while holding their sword vertically. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (L) and other officials attend to a Republican Guard who fainted while standing at attention, as he waits the arrival of Slovakia’s President at the Elysee Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume Saligot / AFP) | Guillaume Saligot / AFP AFP The post Two French Guards Collapse As Macron Welcomes Slovak President appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon: Displaced families struggle to cope
item.description: In Lebanon, more than 360,000 people are still displaced after months of war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to the UN. Along the border, the Israeli army claims to be fighting the Iran-backed militant group but now occupies 6 percent of Lebanese territory and is wiping entire villages off the map. In the border area, we meet families living in makeshift housing. Many fear they may never go home.

item.title: Throwing cow dung: Diwali celebrations take an unusual turn in southern India
item.description: The third day of Diwali was marked in a memorable way on Wednesday in Gummatapura, a hamlet located in India's Tamil Nadu state. Local men and boys threw cow dung at each other to celebrate the festival of Gorehabba which honours Lord Beereshwara, a God worshipped by locals. Believed to be around 300 years old, the festival attracts tourists from across India and further afield.

item.title: CD Projekt Red Will Use AI to Bring Back Geralt’s Original Voice
item.description: In 2019, Jacek Rozenek, the Polish voice actor for Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher games, suffered a stroke that greatly affected his speech. He underwent extensive training to recuperate and regain his ability to act. However, the changes in his voice were still noticeable. To keep the same voice actor in the upcoming DLC Songs of the Past, CD Projekt Red decided to use AI to match his current voice to the original and create the best possible replica.

item.title: European tech buyers add digital sovereignty to cyber shopping list
item.description: European tech buyers are increasingly choosing cybersecurity vendors from their own continent in a bid to reduce their reliance on American technology. Digital sovereignty isn't only prompting enterprise customers to question their clouds of choice, it is also reshaping other parts of the industry too, and the shift is marked. According to sales figures compiled by Context, distributor sales in EMEA of cybersecurity products from EU-headquartered vendors jumped 35 percent in the two years to calendar Q3 2026. Total cybersecurity sales grew up 10 percent over the same period, and sales by US-run companies went up just 8 percent. That growth is from a relatively small base, though EU vendors gained nearly three percentage points to reach 15 percent of tracked sales by value. There is still a long way to go as US-headquartered vendors accounted for 62 percent. The trend coincides with a loss of trust in the Trump administration among customers outside of America, after it cosied up to autocratic rulers while criticizing and punishing allies with tariffs and more. Context stopped short of assigning blame. It said organizations are reviewing their reliance on third-party tech in light of EU compliance regimes: the NIS2 Directive and Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). NIS2, transposed into national law in October 2024 , requires organizations in the bloc to raise their common level of security in the face of digital threats and risks to critical infrastructure. DORA, introduced in January last year, is designed to strengthen cyber security in the financial sector. "Digital sovereignty is becoming a buying decision. As customers and resellers get clearer about what it means in practice, they're asking who holds the encryption keys, who can access sensitive logs and where that data is stored," said Context veep of research Joe Turner. "We're seeing a measurable shift in the EMEA channel. EU vendors gained nearly three points of sales share in two years. An organization can keep its existing identity platform and still choose a European supplier to manage its security logs. That's the kind of decision that gives European vendors an opening." The stats indicate that EU-HQd vendors comprised 92 percent of tracked sales in security awareness training, 82 percent in vulnerability management, and 52 percent for SIEM and log management. US-headquartered companies held into 74 percent of identity and access management sales and 54 percent of cloud security sales. The Reg has asked Context for UK-specific figures to see whether British customers are also voting with their wallets for European alternatives. That certainly isn’t the case for tech purchases in the British public sector, despite Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s professed desire to buy British. Data released yesterday by the Institute for Public Policy Research showed just £1 in every £6 spent by government with the biggest technology suppliers goes to Brit businesses. The trend coincides with a loss of trust in the Trump administration among customers outside of America, after it cosied up to autocratic rulers while criticizing and punishing allies with tariffs and more. Context stopped short of assigning blame. It said organizations are reviewing their reliance on third-party tech in light of EU compliance regimes: the NIS2 Directive and Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). NIS2, transposed into national law in October 2024 , requires organizations in the bloc to raise their common level of security in the face of digital threats and risks to critical infrastructure. DORA, introduced in January last year, is designed to strengthen cyber security in the financial sector. "Digital sovereignty is becoming a buying decision. As customers and resellers get clearer about what it means in practice, they're asking who holds the encryption keys, who can access sensitive logs and where that data is stored," said Context veep of research Joe Turner. "We're seeing a measurable shift in the EMEA channel. EU vendors gained nearly three points of sales share in two years. An organization can keep its existing identity platform and still choose a European supplier to manage its security logs. That's the kind of decision that gives European vendors an opening." The stats indicate that EU-HQd vendors comprised 92 percent of tracked sales in security awareness training, 82 percent in vulnerability management, and 52 percent for SIEM and log management. US-headquartered companies held into 74 percent of identity and access management sales and 54 percent of cloud security sales. The Reg has asked Context for UK-specific figures to see whether British customers are also voting with their wallets for European alternatives. That certainly isn’t the case for tech purchases in the British public sector, despite Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s professed desire to buy British. Data released yesterday by the Institute for Public Policy Research showed just £1 in every £6 spent by government with the biggest technology suppliers goes to Brit businesses. Still, Burnham only came to power in July so there is time yet for him to put his money where his mouth is. Sovereign AI is another area of concern for enterprise customers. Analyst Omdia said last month that despite the marketing adjective meaning "local assets," almost a third AI providers disclose no proof of sovereignty, and some "expect enterprise to pay for audits to verify their claims." Omdia also found that 80 percent of contracts say network resilience is "out of providers control or responsibility," and "US-headquartered AI providers offer better service transparency and contract terms than a majority of local sovereign AI providers, with providers in India a notable exception." Sovereign services in Omdia's classification include data residency, operational autonomy, jurisdictional sovereignty, and technological autonomy. "Local hosting is not sovereignty. Serious providers must demonstrate their credibility through transparent operations, fair contracts and proof of competence. That includes the network, because data in transit must be sovereign too," said Camille Mendler, research director for telco B2B at Omdia. Someone should tell Microsoft and Anthropic . ®

item.title: Nvidia board meets over Jensen Huang’s future after affair revelations
item.description: CEO Jensen Huang’s future with Nvidia was unclear Thursday as the chip giant’s board was reported to have met after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion dollar behemoth plunging and left uncertain the fate of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom. Huang, 63, has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China, and US President Donald Trump last year cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export there over objections from Beijing’s critics in both parties. The chip giant’s board met on Wednesday to weigh Huang’s future, according to CNN and the New York Times. Nvidia has not made any statements about the outcome of the meeting. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Nvidia shares were down around 25 percent from their all-time high in early October and the scandal has raised questions over who could replace Huang if he is ousted. The rapidly unfolding story exploded after reports that Huang, who has been married to Lori Huang for over 40 years, was involved in an extramarital romance. The Nvidia CEO has since admitted to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Alice Huang was among the attendees at a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. She visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Nvidia’s board had already announced on Sunday a probe of what it called reporting that Jensen Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort”. Then came on Wednesday New York Times reporting that the Nvidia co-founder was involved in a second extramarital affair, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The chip giant’s code of conduct tells associates to avoid conflicts of interest, and cites the example of “personal relationships”. “We avoid situations where our actions might create a conflict — actual or potential — between our personal gain and our obligations to Nvidia”, the code says. – Possible ouster – Nvidia’s bylaws require a majority of the 11 board directors to remove Huang as CEO. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion dollar behemoth plunging and left uncertain the fate of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom. Huang, 63, has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China, and US President Donald Trump last year cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export there over objections from Beijing’s critics in both parties. The chip giant’s board met on Wednesday to weigh Huang’s future, according to CNN and the New York Times. Nvidia has not made any statements about the outcome of the meeting. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Nvidia shares were down around 25 percent from their all-time high in early October and the scandal has raised questions over who could replace Huang if he is ousted. The rapidly unfolding story exploded after reports that Huang, who has been married to Lori Huang for over 40 years, was involved in an extramarital romance. The Nvidia CEO has since admitted to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Alice Huang was among the attendees at a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. She visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Nvidia’s board had already announced on Sunday a probe of what it called reporting that Jensen Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort”. Then came on Wednesday New York Times reporting that the Nvidia co-founder was involved in a second extramarital affair, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The chip giant’s code of conduct tells associates to avoid conflicts of interest, and cites the example of “personal relationships”. “We avoid situations where our actions might create a conflict — actual or potential — between our personal gain and our obligations to Nvidia”, the code says. – Possible ouster – Nvidia’s bylaws require a majority of the 11 board directors to remove Huang as CEO. But he would retain his board seat, which could only be taken away by shareholders. Several directors want to appoint Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim leader, according to US news outlet Semafor. An outside firm is helping the board identify potential replacements, Bloomberg News reported. Huang has repeatedly avoided naming a successor when the question is brought up. The New York Times earlier reported that the tech CEO has been called on by Congress to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang. As the artificial intelligence industry surge has spurred Nvidia’s stock prices to new heights, Huang has appeared at US President Donald Trump’s side at White House events, as recently as last month when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader. Huang was among the world’s most influential tech leaders — including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg — who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity. Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. Founded in 1993, Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). Nvidia’s processors are mostly made by Taiwanese company TSMC, the world’s largest contract manufacturer of chips. Nvidia is scheduled to release its quarterly results on November 17. item.title: SQI College of ICT announces second convocation for November 21
item.description: SQI College of ICT has announced November 21, 2026, for its second convocation ceremony, with a focus on the growing influence of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital skills in shaping the future. The ceremony, scheduled to begin at 10:00 a.m. at the institution’s main campus along Old Ilorin Road, opposite Yoaco Filling Station, Ogbomoso, Oyo State, will bring together graduating students, academics, technology professionals, industry leaders and other stakeholders. The event will be held under the theme, “Audacity to Reimagine the Future with Artificial Intelligence, Digital Skills and Human Possibilities.” The institution said the theme reflects the transformative impact of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies on society, while highlighting the need to combine technological advancement with human creativity, innovation and relevant skills to shape the future. The ceremony is expected to attract personalities from various sectors, including academics, technology experts, industry leaders and professionals. Graduating students, parents, guardians, members of the Governing Council and Board of Trustees are also expected to attend. Established to bridge the gap between conventional education and industry demands, SQI College of ICT has continued to emphasise practical learning, hands-on training and industry-relevant skills development. The institution said its academic approach goes beyond conventional classroom instruction to incorporate real-world projects, practical assignments and experiential learning aimed at equipping students with the skills to address industry challenges and compete in the global digital economy. Its academic offerings include Computer Science + AI, Accountancy + AI, and Business Administration and Management + AI, alongside specialised training in Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Data Analysis, Cybersecurity, Visual Design, Product Design and Cloud Computing. Through these programmes, the institution seeks to produce graduates capable of translating theoretical knowledge into practical solutions, developing technology-driven products and contributing to the digital transformation of businesses and society. Beyond the conferment of academic awards, the second convocation is expected to provide opportunities for networking, knowledge exchange and collaboration among academics, industry professionals, technology enthusiasts and emerging talents. The Rector, on behalf of the Governing Council and Board of Trustees, has invited parents, industry partners, members of the public and well-wishers to join the institution in celebrating the graduating students and the milestone in its development. The institution said the ceremony would further demonstrate its commitment to technology education, digital skills development and the preparation of a new generation of professionals for opportunities in the global digital economy. item.title: Withheld ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌​‍‍⁠​​‌​LG funds: Osun workers resume after three-day warning strike
item.description: Government workers in Osun resumed duty on Thursday after putting off their three-day warning strike called by the organiser labour for the release of funds due to local governments in the state by the Federal Government. The News of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the gates of the state government secretariat in Abere and Osun Assembly, shut since Monday, were reopened with workers back to work. Similarly, workers in Olorunda and Osogbo Local Government Secretariats were also back to their duty posts. NAN reports that organised labour in the state had on Sunday directed workers to embarked on solidarity strike with local government workers for the release of the withheld council allocations. The organised labour comprising the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Trade Union Congress (TUC) and Joint Negotiating Council (JNC), however, on Wednesday directed workers to resume duty today. The organised labour appreciated workers, pensioners and affiliate unions for their support, cooperation and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “The organised labour expresses its profound appreciation to all affiliate unions, workers, pensioners and members for their unwavering solidarity, cooperation and exemplary conduct throughout the three-day sympathy strike in support of the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE), Osun Council. “We commend all members for their commitment, discipline, unity and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “Your solidarity has once again demonstrated the strength of the labour movement and our collective resolve to defend workers’ rights, welfare and dignity. “Accordingly, all workers are hereby directed to resume work at midnight Nov. 11. “All affiliate unions and their members are enjoined to comply fully with this directive and return to their respective workplaces,” it said. The organised labour urged workers to remain calm, united and steadfast, while maintaining mobilisation and remaining on standby for further directives. (NAN) The post Withheld ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌​‍‍⁠​​‌​LG funds: Osun workers resume after three-day warning strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rockstar workers vote on union recognition as GTA VI launch looms
item.description: More than 1,600 Rockstar Games employees in the UK will begin voting on union recognition on Thursday, with the ballot kicking off just a week before the long-awaited launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The ballot, which opens on November 12 and runs until November 26, will determine whether Rockstar formally recognizes the Rockstar Game Workers Union, part of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Nearly all UK employees below director level are eligible to vote. If successful, the union would become the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, giving workers a collective voice. The proposed recognition agreement follows four months of negotiations between Rockstar management and employees. It would allow workers to negotiate over pay, overtime, pensions, bonuses, leave and other employment conditions, while securing consultation rights over HR policies and AI. The vote comes at a particularly busy time for Rockstar, with GTA VI finally due to arrive on November 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. The game is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history, although the people responsible for making it have rather more immediate concerns than sales records. "I am incredibly proud of the work we've put into making this game. I'm also proud of the union we've built here. For me, those two things are connected," said Nestor Uriate, an animation programmer and Rockstar Game Workers Union representative. "We care deeply about the games we make, and we want to make sure we can continue doing that work in an environment where we're respected, have a meaningful say over our conditions and can feel secure about our futures." The vote follows a year of bad blood between Rockstar and the IWGB. The union accused the GTA developer of union busting after it fired 31 members in October 2025, claiming they had been singled out for taking part in a private Discord group. Rockstar denied the allegations, insisting the workers were dismissed for gross misconduct rather than their union activities. The dispute subsequently reached an employment tribunal, where Rockstar unsuccessfully attempted to have blacklisting allegations struck from the case . Closing submissions are expected on November 17 and 18, meaning the legal proceedings will reach their final stages just as GTA VI prepares to hit shelves. item.dc:creator: Carly Page
item.content:encoded: More than 1,600 Rockstar Games employees in the UK will begin voting on union recognition on Thursday, with the ballot kicking off just a week before the long-awaited launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The ballot, which opens on November 12 and runs until November 26, will determine whether Rockstar formally recognizes the Rockstar Game Workers Union, part of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Nearly all UK employees below director level are eligible to vote. If successful, the union would become the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, giving workers a collective voice. The proposed recognition agreement follows four months of negotiations between Rockstar management and employees. It would allow workers to negotiate over pay, overtime, pensions, bonuses, leave and other employment conditions, while securing consultation rights over HR policies and AI. The vote comes at a particularly busy time for Rockstar, with GTA VI finally due to arrive on November 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. The game is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history, although the people responsible for making it have rather more immediate concerns than sales records. "I am incredibly proud of the work we've put into making this game. I'm also proud of the union we've built here. For me, those two things are connected," said Nestor Uriate, an animation programmer and Rockstar Game Workers Union representative. "We care deeply about the games we make, and we want to make sure we can continue doing that work in an environment where we're respected, have a meaningful say over our conditions and can feel secure about our futures." The vote follows a year of bad blood between Rockstar and the IWGB. The union accused the GTA developer of union busting after it fired 31 members in October 2025, claiming they had been singled out for taking part in a private Discord group. Rockstar denied the allegations, insisting the workers were dismissed for gross misconduct rather than their union activities. The dispute subsequently reached an employment tribunal, where Rockstar unsuccessfully attempted to have blacklisting allegations struck from the case . Closing submissions are expected on November 17 and 18, meaning the legal proceedings will reach their final stages just as GTA VI prepares to hit shelves. Despite the ongoing dispute, Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, recently indicated that management would respect the outcome of the recognition vote, telling Bloomberg : "We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union." The union campaign has also attracted support from elsewhere in the games industry, including SAG-AFTRA and the Communications Workers of America (CWA), which represents workers at Blizzard. Alex Marshall, president of the IWGB, said the vote was an opportunity for Rockstar employees to take greater control over their working conditions. "What happens at Rockstar matters beyond the studio. Workers across the games industry are watching, and this ballot is an opportunity to show what can be achieved when people come together, organize and build the collective power to shape their own working lives." For Rockstar, November was already shaping up to be a big month. By the time GTA VI has been in players' hands for a week, the company should also know whether its UK workforce has voted to secure a formal seat at the negotiating table. ®

item.title: NHS England deletes ‘misleading’ claim 137 trusts benefiting from Palantir AI tools
item.description: Exclusive: The Guardian revealed 29 hospital trusts were not or hardly using the controversial patient data tech NHS England has deleted a claim from its website stating 137 hospital trusts are benefiting from Palantir’s AI health data system after the Guardian revealed 29 of them were not using all or most of the controversial technology. Health bosses had published a list of all the NHS bodies “live” with and “realising benefits” from the AI-powered federated data platform (FDP), a system set up to improve patient outcomes, boost operating theatre efficiency and speed up bed discharges. But after 29 trusts said it was either not live or they were not using any of its applications, the original list of hospitals appears to have been taken down. Continue reading...

item.title: Datacentres are deeply unpopular. Has Sweden made one we can all love?
item.description: It is built of wood, resembles an Ikea and its power is totally renewable. Plus, it was built with the local community in mind. Is this facility in Falun the best datacentre in the world? ‘It was pretty cool, when they were building it. It looked like a very large Ikea,” says John Wernvik, of EcoDataCenter. He is giving me a tour of their facility in Falun, Sweden, which could lay claim to being the world’s greenest datacentre – although to many, that is a contradiction in terms. One difference is immediately visible: this datacentre is made out of wood. Huge panels of cross-laminated timber arrived at the site pre-cut, and were assembled by crane according to instructions, like flatpack furniture. Aesthetically, this section of the datacentre is more like an Ikea before the fit-out, a cavernous, echoey, immaculately clean hangar. The wood is not EcoDataCenter’s only claim to sustainability; it is more than just cosmetic, says Wernvik, the company’s chief external relations and sustainability officer. “Compared with a traditional datacentre built with steel and concrete, we lower the embodied carbon of the full structure by three times.” With a complex the size of a football pitch, that is a lot of wood, but, says Wernvik, “the amount of timber one of our datacentres uses takes the Swedish forest about 10 to 15 minutes to grow back”. Continue reading...

item.title: Sales Hack Conference 2026: Nnamani leads six industry experts to Abuja
item.description: By Chioma Okoye The Convener of the Sales Hack Conference, Chinedu Paul Nnamani, is set to bring together six professionals from the business, technology, entrepreneurship, media and management sectors for the 2026 edition of the conference scheduled to hold in Abuja on Saturday, November 14. The conference, themed “Explosive Sales: Market Smart, Convert More, Earn Big,” is aimed at equipping entrepreneurs, business owners, marketers and sales professionals with practical strategies for improving sales performance, attracting customers and growing sustainable businesses. The event is expected to attract business owners, corporate professionals, students and other stakeholders for discussions on sales strategies, market positioning, customer psychology and business growth. According to the organisers, the conference is designed to provide a platform for sharing practical business knowledge, professional experience and industry insights to help individuals and organisations strengthen their sales capabilities. The 2026 edition will feature speakers drawn from different areas of the business and professional ecosystem. They include Dr. Jamie Pajoel, Founder and Global President of Jamie Pajoel International; Kel Armstrong Amobi, Founder and Host of KaaTruths Podcast; Dr. Ninnah Samuel, a business and technology law expert; Ajah Excel, Chief Executive Officer of Silicon Africa and Convener of SMfest; and Abraham Ofure Orukpe, a business management consultant and coach. Nnamani will also feature as convener, coordinating the engagement between the speakers and participants. The organisers said the diversity of the speakers was intended to provide participants with perspectives on different aspects of sales development, including business strategy, technology, communication, consumer behaviour, legal considerations and management. Discussions will focus on practical sales techniques, buying behaviour, customer acquisition and retention, relationship building, revenue generation and strategies for competing in an increasingly demanding marketplace. The conference is also expected to provide networking opportunities for entrepreneurs, corporate professionals and emerging talents to establish business relationships and explore potential collaborations. The organisers said the event would be particularly relevant to Nigerian businesses navigating changing consumer expectations, increasing market competition and the need to develop sustainable revenue streams. The conference will hold at Centre Point Event Centre, Centre Shehu Shagari Way, Wuse, Abuja, beginning at 8 a.m. West Africa Time. Registration is available under four categories: Basic, N5,000; Executive, N15,000; Premium, N30,000; and VIP, N70,000. Further information and registration are available through the conference’s official website. The organisers said the event was part of efforts to promote knowledge sharing, professional development and improved sales capabilities among Nigerian business

item.title: Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick
item.description: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him. Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone. “Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach,” the club said in a statement. It added: “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.” Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away and was looking to the international break as usual. But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins in all competitions. Former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago. The Red Devils, once the dominant force in English football, have been overtaken by Manchester City, Liverpool and Arsenal. United’s next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. The post Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Five key allies of Peter Obi who parted ways with him after 2023
item.description: ‎ The recent decision by Yunusa Tanko a leading figure in the Obidient Movement, to accept an appointment as Director-General of the presidential campaign council of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) candidate has once again drawn attention to the growing list of notable political associates who have distanced themselves from former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi. ‎ ‎Since the conclusion of the 2023 presidential election, Obi has remained one of the country’s most influential opposition politicians. ‎However, several key figures who played important roles in his campaign, political structure, or movement have either left the Labour Party, aligned with other political interests, or openly criticized his political direction. Obi is presently the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 election. ‎ ‎These defections have triggered renewed debate about the cohesion of the political movement that emerged around Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign. 2027: IGP warns officers against compromise Thugs attack Pantami’s campaign rally in Gombe ‎ ‎While Obi continues to command a loyal support base across the country, the departure of several high-profile associates underscores the challenge of maintaining political unity and building a durable structure ahead of the next electoral cycle. ‎ However, his present alliance with Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the leader of Kwankwasiyya Movement, is seen by many as a plus to him. ‎ ‎Below are five of such most prominent names. ‎ ‎ YUNUSA TANKO tanko yunusa ‎ ‎Perhaps the latest and most symbolic departure is that of Yunusa Tanko, who served as National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and was one of the most visible defenders of Obi after the 2023 election. ‎ ‎Tanko was a key mobiliser of Obi’s support base across the country and regularly represented the movement on national television and at political events. However, he recently accepted an appointment as Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council of SDP presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, effectively moving away from Obi’s political camp. ‎ ‎YUSUF DATTI BABA-AHMED ‎ ‎As Obi’s running mate in the 2023 election, Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed was one of the central figures of the Labour Party ticket. ‎Although he has not openly defected to another political camp in the manner of some of Obi’s former associates, reports indicate that he publicly expressed disagreements with aspects of Obi’s political direction, fueling speculation about differences within the former presidential ticket. ‎ ‎KENNETH OKONKWO ‎ ‎Actor, lawyer and politician, Kenneth Okonkwo was one of the most vocal spokespersons of the Obi campaign during the 2023 presidential race. ‎ ‎In July 2024, he announced his exit from the Labour Party and openly criticized Obi’s handling of the party’s leadership crisis. However, he recently accepted an appointment as Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council of SDP presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, effectively moving away from Obi’s political camp. ‎ ‎YUSUF DATTI BABA-AHMED ‎ ‎As Obi’s running mate in the 2023 election, Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed was one of the central figures of the Labour Party ticket. ‎Although he has not openly defected to another political camp in the manner of some of Obi’s former associates, reports indicate that he publicly expressed disagreements with aspects of Obi’s political direction, fueling speculation about differences within the former presidential ticket. ‎ ‎KENNETH OKONKWO ‎ ‎Actor, lawyer and politician, Kenneth Okonkwo was one of the most vocal spokespersons of the Obi campaign during the 2023 presidential race. ‎ ‎In July 2024, he announced his exit from the Labour Party and openly criticized Obi’s handling of the party’s leadership crisis. Okonkwo said he had lost confidence in Obi’s ability to build a strong political platform capable of challenging the ruling party. ‎ ‎The disagreement later deepened, with Okonkwo becoming one of Obi’s most outspoken critics and subsequently aligning politically with former Vice President Atiku Abubakar. ‎ VALENTINE OZIGBO ‎ ‎Businessman and politician, Valentine Ozigbo, was one of Obi’s closest political allies in Anambra State and joined the Labour Party ahead of the 2023 elections to support Obi’s presidential bid. ‎ ‎However, in February 2025, Ozigbo resigned from the party, saying recent developments had convinced him that it was time to pursue a different political path. He later joined the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). Although he informed Obi of his decision and spoke respectfully of him, the move marked a significant loss for Obi’s political structure in Anambra. ‎ ‎ISAAC BALAMI ‎ ‎Isaac Balami served as Deputy Campaign Manager of the Obi-Datti presidential campaign and was regarded as one of the key northern figures in the organisation. ‎ ‎Following the election, Balami moved away from Obi’s political fold and later aligned himself with the ruling APC, adding to the list of former campaign insiders who chose a different political direction.

item.title: Millions join Spain's first general strike in 14 years as anger over housing leads to clashes
item.description: A general strike by 4 million Spanish workers — around one-fifth of the total workforce — against the country's housing crisis was mostly peaceful on Wednesday, unions said, though by the evening clashes erupted in some areas of Barcelona and Madrid. It is ‌the first general strike since workers downed tools in 2012 against austerity measures during the euro zone debt crisis.

item.title: 'Peruvian pope' makes jubilant return to his second 'homeland'
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in his "beloved" Peru on Wednesday, a nostalgic return to the nation where he spent two decades as a missionary before being tapped to lead the world's 1.4 billion Catholics. The 71-year-old pontiff landed in Lima on the last leg of an arduous three-nation Latin American tour, just weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: Mississippi elects Democrat Colom as state's first post-Civil War Black senator
item.description: Democratic nominee Scott Colom defeated Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday in Mississippi's closely contested US Senate race after a prolonged ballot counting process, giving the state its first Black US senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction. Colom's narrow victory is a seismic shift in Mississippi, which has been controlled mostly by white conservatives for generations despite having the largest share of Black residents of any US state.

item.title: Two dead, several injured after New York building collapses
item.description: Two people were killed Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in New York, city authorities said. The building fell into a neighboring excavation site, trapping several people who firefighters worked to free over several hours using drones, search dogs and chainsaws.

item.title: Orbit Global Menu: A working global menu addon for GNOME
item.description: A new extension brings a working global menu bar to the GNOME desktop, even for some apps that don’t have menu bars at all. Orbit Global Menu is a new GNOME extension that gives the GNOME desktop a feature it was intentionally designed without, and one that some users miss very badly – this vulture being one of them. It adds a working global menu bar to the GNOME top panel. We suspect this is something that will cause strongly contrasting opinions among many GNOME users: some will by puzzled why anyone would bother, while others may think "at last!" and rush to try it. There have been other attempts to do this before, and the Reg FOSS desk has tried several of them, but we never found one that worked with the majority of applications. Our fondness for this UI feature was visible in the two-part series we wrote in September on how to customize Xfce and then in part two how to get the global menu working with more apps. The problem is getting worse over time, as in recent versions (since GNOME 40 and Gtk4), the GNOME human-interface guidelines encourage smartphone-style hamburger menus, replacing the traditional horizontal menu bar. It is tricky to add global menu bar support to apps that lack a menu bar, but Orbit's developer "Unmade" found a rather labor-intensive solution. The menu bar applet contains maps of keyboard controls for 292 different apps, so it can show a menu all on its own and then send those apps simulated keystrokes to operate it. It's not the programs' full menu trees, just a subset of them, but it works. It's also not the most elegant solution, but it is a solution and it works. We tried it on Ubuntu 26.10 and every app in the full install worked to at least some extent. If you are willing and able to build and install a small additional connector, it lets the global-menu applet talk to lots more applications. The GNOME shell is unusual among open source desktop environments, to an extent that we have criticized before. GNOME Shell was designed with a distinctive look and feel of its own, unlike almost all other desktops. It has a minimalist, stripped-down layout that doesn't look or work quite like anything else, and it's intentionally not very customizable. To change how GNOME works means writing new Javascript code, then packaging it as an extension that users can install from the GNOME Extensions website. This requires both a browser extension and a "native host messaging" connector to be installed into the underlying OS – or a purpose-written app. By default, the desktop comes with neither. The end result is that GNOME lends a visual identity to the Linux desktop, one that is clear and distinct from either Windows or macOS. (Back in 2013, this vulture argued that when Microsoft threatened to sue multiple Linux vendors over infringing Windows UI patents, some 20 years ago, this UI fragmentation was just what the company wanted .) GNOME 2 was the Linux world's default desktop. GNOME Shell was controversial in its early days,
item.dc:creator: Liam Proven
item.content:encoded: A new extension brings a working global menu bar to the GNOME desktop, even for some apps that don’t have menu bars at all. Orbit Global Menu is a new GNOME extension that gives the GNOME desktop a feature it was intentionally designed without, and one that some users miss very badly – this vulture being one of them. It adds a working global menu bar to the GNOME top panel. We suspect this is something that will cause strongly contrasting opinions among many GNOME users: some will by puzzled why anyone would bother, while others may think "at last!" and rush to try it. There have been other attempts to do this before, and the Reg FOSS desk has tried several of them, but we never found one that worked with the majority of applications. Our fondness for this UI feature was visible in the two-part series we wrote in September on how to customize Xfce and then in part two how to get the global menu working with more apps. The problem is getting worse over time, as in recent versions (since GNOME 40 and Gtk4), the GNOME human-interface guidelines encourage smartphone-style hamburger menus, replacing the traditional horizontal menu bar. It is tricky to add global menu bar support to apps that lack a menu bar, but Orbit's developer "Unmade" found a rather labor-intensive solution. The menu bar applet contains maps of keyboard controls for 292 different apps, so it can show a menu all on its own and then send those apps simulated keystrokes to operate it. It's not the programs' full menu trees, just a subset of them, but it works. It's also not the most elegant solution, but it is a solution and it works. We tried it on Ubuntu 26.10 and every app in the full install worked to at least some extent. If you are willing and able to build and install a small additional connector, it lets the global-menu applet talk to lots more applications. The GNOME shell is unusual among open source desktop environments, to an extent that we have criticized before. GNOME Shell was designed with a distinctive look and feel of its own, unlike almost all other desktops. It has a minimalist, stripped-down layout that doesn't look or work quite like anything else, and it's intentionally not very customizable. To change how GNOME works means writing new Javascript code, then packaging it as an extension that users can install from the GNOME Extensions website. This requires both a browser extension and a "native host messaging" connector to be installed into the underlying OS – or a purpose-written app. By default, the desktop comes with neither. The end result is that GNOME lends a visual identity to the Linux desktop, one that is clear and distinct from either Windows or macOS. (Back in 2013, this vulture argued that when Microsoft threatened to sue multiple Linux vendors over infringing Windows UI patents, some 20 years ago, this UI fragmentation was just what the company wanted .) GNOME 2 was the Linux world's default desktop. GNOME Shell was controversial in its early days, and lost pole position, but it has since won it back. Today, GNOME is the default desktop on all the major distros: Ubuntu, Fedora and Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the RHELatives, as well as Debian and SUSE, all default to GNOME. GNOME does away with a lot of features that are significant functional parts of other graphical desktops. For instance, it has no desktop icons, no system tray or defined place for status indicators, and neither GNOME nor GNOME-compliant applications have menu bars, either inside windows (Microsoft style) or in the top panel (Apple macOS style). This is disorienting and confusing for those used to controlling software mainly using their menus – but now, that's mainly older hands. This design suits those who grew up on smartphones and tablets, or who feel more comfortable with their stripped-back keyboardless UI than a full desktop WIMP, which can be overwhelming to newbies and non-techies. If you've followed the evolution of graphical desktops for some 40 years, as this gray-plumed vulture has, some trends are very apparent that aren't so clear if you came in once evolution was underway. Apple introduced the first global menu bar in the Lisa, and improved on that in the Macintosh. DR GEM copied it very early on , but Apple sued and DR changed the PC version of GEM to be less Mac-like. Microsoft's Windows came along after this, and moved menu bars inside windows instead. When Apple acquired NeXT in 1996 , it moved NeXTstep's patent-avoidant vertical menus back to a global bar at the top, along with the clock and some status indicators. There they remain, 30 years later. In 2007, it launched the iPhone, containing a very cut-down OS based on OS X, replacing the Finder with a cut-down version of the Dashboard layer from OS X 10.4 . The panel remained, shorn of its menus, which were too fiddly for a small screen. As The Register mentioned in 2017 , in its preliminary releases, Android started out as a keypad-driven Java phone that looked and worked very much like BlackBerry. When the iPhone appeared, Google changed course . The new Android UI resembled iOS, complete with that top panel, still without menus. GNOME 3.0 was not far behind: in 2009 the team promised a revamp of the user experience, and in 2011, launched GNOME 3.0. It too has the fixed top panel — now huge on a laptop or desktop landscape screen – and mostly empty. Now that top panel regains its original 1983 function. We're rather impressed by the Orbit global menu. It does the job, and it even works with apps that don't have menu bars. It's not perfect: for instance, over-long menus have to scroll, and may fail to do so if new submenus appear. The GitHub repository has extensive instructions, including how to build and install the optional connector module that lets more apps export their real menus to the extension. It also tells you how to instruct some apps, notably Firefox, that there is a global menu for it to use. We are saddened to note that, as is so often the case, Wayland gets in the way here. It works rather well with some other extensions, too. With a menu bar, GNOME's strangely centered clock seems out of place, but several extensions, such as F rippery Move Clock , shove it over to the right where we still feel it belongs. If you prefer a lighter-colored panel and dock, it also plays nicely with Blur my Shell . ®

item.title: Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support
item.description: The Angola Embassy in Nigeria has commended Nigeria’s support for the country’s independence, attained in 1975. Dr José Zau, Angola’s Head of Mission to Nigeria, Benin, Niger and ECOWAS, said this at the celebration of the 51st anniversary of independence on Wednesday night in Abuja. Zau described relations between the two countries as a strategic, historic and fraternal partnership, anchored in political alignment as leading African oil producers. He said Nigeria played a significant role in supporting Angola’s independence process and the consolidation of the Angolan state. “Through the Bilateral Joint Commission, the two nations have been updating and expanding dozens of agreements and memoranda of understanding. “These cover trade, transport, culture, professional training, defence and public order, cybersecurity, and academic exchange,” he said. He cited a visa-exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and twinning partnerships between Angolan provinces and Nigerian states, as measures to deepen ties. The twinning pairs the Namibe and Bengo provinces with the Bayelsa and Nasarawa states, he said. He said relations were strengthened by engagement between Angolan President João Lourenço and Nigerian President Bola Tinubu. Zau said the Caculo Cabaça Dam would become operational in June 2027, with the capacity to generate at least 2,172 megawatts (MW). He said the dam would raise Angola’s total capacity from 6,400 MW to about 8,600 MW. He also highlighted the country’s achievements in 2026. (NAN) The post Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Thursday said diplomacy should resume “without further delay” to end the US-Iran war after talks with his Iranian counterpart. Erdogan met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN climate conference in the Turkish province of Antalya, his office said. During their discussion, Erdogan underscored “the importance of getting to the negotiating table without further delay” and said Turkey would continue to support efforts aimed at securing peace. “Common ground for agreement must be strengthened and diplomacy given a chance,” he said, expressing hope that the conflict with the US “would end as soon as possible”. The Middle East war broke out on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the fray. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian leaves after delivering a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP In an address to the UN climate summit on Wednesday, Pezeshkian accused the United States and Israel of inflicting severe environmental damage during attacks on the Islamic Republic. “The recent criminal and illegal aggression against Iran by America and the Zionist regime… has inflicted severe damage on the environment, releasing massive quantities of pollutants and greenhouse gases into the atmosphere,” he said. Diplomatic efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan have sought to negotiate an end to the war. Tehran wants Washington to accept a raft of demands including unfreezing assets and lifting sanctions in return for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the vital energy conduit it has blockaded since the start of the conflict. AFP The post Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: APC Is Working Towards Coronation, Not Election, ADC Ologbondiyan On Court Voiding Atiku’s Candidacy
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has described the court’s voidance of its principal presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as an attempt to silence the voices of opposition parties, alleging that the ruling party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), was working to present its candidate, Bola Tinubu, as the sole candidate in the coming 2027 general elections. Justice Lifu, on November 5, nullified the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC and declared invalid the actions taken by the caretaker committee. The ruling followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the committee assumed leadership after the resignation of former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu. The court’s decision was reported to have affected the process that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate, as the Mark-led committee organised the primary election. The ADC, however, rejected the judgment, describing it as legally indefensible and accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of seeking to weaken the opposition. The party also said it would challenge the decision, citing an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, which it said had affirmed the legitimacy of the Mark-led leadership. A combo of NDC Lawyer, Kalu Kalu, and Atiku Abubakar. Speaking further on ADC’s standpoint on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Kola Ologbondiyan, Spokesperson of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, accused the APC of working toward coronating Tinubu in 2027 instead of allowing for healthy competition. Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC has given no room for opposition politics. “So it now goes into what we have been saying because what we now want is that no candidate must stand against during the election, and that goes to nothing as far as we are concerned in the African Democratic Congress.” The ADC’s Spokesperson said that his party has taken the necessary steps to appeal the judgement. “We are sure that we will go to the next level in the administration of justice; we believe that all this manipulation and attempt to suppress Nigerians, all this move to dismantle democratic structures will not work. We have seen it over and over again; it will not stand.” He alleged that the APC is working to ensure that the ADC candidate, Abubakar, is not on the ballot for the 2027 election, and to enthrone President Tinubu as a life president. “I want Nigerians to know, anyone thinking that this is about ADC is not reading the processes well. item.content:encoded: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has described the court’s voidance of its principal presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as an attempt to silence the voices of opposition parties, alleging that the ruling party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), was working to present its candidate, Bola Tinubu, as the sole candidate in the coming 2027 general elections. Justice Lifu, on November 5, nullified the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC and declared invalid the actions taken by the caretaker committee. The ruling followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the committee assumed leadership after the resignation of former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu. The court’s decision was reported to have affected the process that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate, as the Mark-led committee organised the primary election. The ADC, however, rejected the judgment, describing it as legally indefensible and accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of seeking to weaken the opposition. The party also said it would challenge the decision, citing an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, which it said had affirmed the legitimacy of the Mark-led leadership. A combo of NDC Lawyer, Kalu Kalu, and Atiku Abubakar. Speaking further on ADC’s standpoint on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Kola Ologbondiyan, Spokesperson of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, accused the APC of working toward coronating Tinubu in 2027 instead of allowing for healthy competition. Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC has given no room for opposition politics. “So it now goes into what we have been saying because what we now want is that no candidate must stand against during the election, and that goes to nothing as far as we are concerned in the African Democratic Congress.” The ADC’s Spokesperson said that his party has taken the necessary steps to appeal the judgement. “We are sure that we will go to the next level in the administration of justice; we believe that all this manipulation and attempt to suppress Nigerians, all this move to dismantle democratic structures will not work. We have seen it over and over again; it will not stand.” He alleged that the APC is working to ensure that the ADC candidate, Abubakar, is not on the ballot for the 2027 election, and to enthrone President Tinubu as a life president. “I want Nigerians to know, anyone thinking that this is about ADC is not reading the processes well. It is about one man who wants to turn himself into a life president” Ologbondiyan argued that the ADC has a subsisting decision from the Federal High Court in Abuja, a court with the same jurisdiction, earlier recognising the leadership of Senator David Mark as chairman of ADC. “The Federal High Court in Abuja here, saying, recognising the leadership of Senator David Mark as chairman of ADC. It’s upon that that the party has carried out its activities.” He described the recent judgment invalidating David Mark as Chairman of ADC as a “hired gun.” “Now you have a hired gun coming from nowhere, sitting in appeal on the same court of the same jurisdiction, and saying that, oh, what his own fellow brother on the bench ruled is no longer valid, when it was the same court that the party obeyed in carrying out its activities. ” Ologbondiyan, however, noted that the party believes in the decision taken by the Court of Appeal. President Bola Tinubu during the inauguration of the APC PCC. On November 6, the party announced that it had filed an appeal and an application for a stay of execution, and cautioned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) against taking consequential action while the legal challenge was pending. A lawyer to the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Kalu Kalu, argued that the judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja does not invalidate Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy for the 2027 presidential election. Kalu made the position known on Wednesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , after the certified true copy (CTC) of the controversial judgment was released earlier in the day. He accused some people of reading into the judgment orders that were not made by the court, insisting that no part of the decision expressly nullified Atiku’s candidacy. “The judgement of Honourable Justice Peter Lifu does not in any way void the candidacy of Atiku Abubakar for the presidential election coming up on the 16th day of January, 2027. There is no portion of that judgement that voids the candidacy of Atiku Abubakar and other candidates of the party, there is none,” Kalu said. He urged Nigerians to read the judgment, arguing that its operative orders were being misrepresented. “And we are placing it on record, let the whole world go and read the judgement of Honourable Justice Peter Lifu. The best you could get from that judgement is a declarative order made by Honourable Justice Peter Lifu that all actions, steps, activities taken by David Mark and Aregbesola from the 29th day of July 2025 till date are null and void and of no effect whatsoever. And people are now importing what is not stated or what is not declared on that judgment,” he added.
